nodes.question: Who needs an account to use the app?

options.label: Nobody logs in — one person uses it on their own device
Exactly one person logs in (the owner)
Several people log in, possibly with different powers

nodes.question: Do different people have different powers?

options.label: Everyone who logs in can do everything
An owner/admin plus staff with fewer powers
Admins define their own roles and permissions

nodes.question: Is this for one business, or will many separate businesses use it with their data kept apart?

options.label: One business (ours)
Many separate businesses, each seeing only its own data

nodes.question: How do additional people get access?

options.label: No additional people
An admin invites them
Anyone can sign up themselves

nodes.question: How do people sign in?

options.label: No sign-in
Email + password
Email link, no password
Google/Microsoft sign-in
Company single sign-on (SAML/OIDC)

nodes.question: What happens when two people edit the same thing at once?

options.label: Rare; the last save wins
Common; the app must prevent or merge conflicting edits

nodes.question: Do you need a record of who changed what and when?

options.label: No
Just created/updated by whom and when
A full, viewable history of every change

nodes.question: How does the app reach people when something happens?

options.label: It doesn't — people check the app
Email
Email and SMS
Only inside the app (bell/inbox)

nodes.question: Must it work without internet?

options.label: Online only
Keeps working offline and syncs later

nodes.question: Where is it used?

options.label: In a browser, on desktop and phone
In a browser, mostly on phones
As an installed phone app
As an installed desktop app

nodes.question: Do you start with existing data?

options.label: Start empty
Import from a spreadsheet/CSV once
Migrate from another tool

nodes.question: Do people need to get their data out?

options.label: No
Download lists as CSV/Excel
Full export and/or an API

nodes.question: When something is deleted, what really happens?

options.label: It's gone
It's archived and can be restored
Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled

nodes.question: How much data will there be?

options.label: Hundreds of records
Tens of thousands
Millions

nodes.question: Does it need to connect to other tools?

options.label: No
A few key ones (e.g., accounting, payments, calendar)
Many — it needs a public API / webhooks

nodes.question: Languages and regions?

options.label: One language, one country
Several languages
Several countries (taxes, formats, currencies)

nodes.question: Can files/photos be attached to things?

options.label: No
Yes — upload and download
Yes — with previews, versions, and sharing

nodes.question: Do some actions need someone else's approval first?

options.label: No
One approver
Multi-step approval chains

nodes.question: Must anything happen automatically on a schedule?

options.label: No
Only reminders/notifications
Records get created automatically (recurring invoices, appointments, reports)

nodes.question: Does it hold data with special legal handling (health, payment cards, minors)?

options.label: Ordinary business data
Personal data needing consent/retention care (GDPR-like)
Regulated data (health, cards, finance)

nodes.question: How long is data kept?

options.label: Until someone deletes it
Auto-removed after a set period
Each business sets its own policy

nodes.question: Can each business customize the app?

options.label: No — everyone gets the same thing
Branding and templates (logo, colors, wording)
Custom fields and workflows

nodes.question: What do people need to see across many records?

options.label: Sortable, filterable lists
A dashboard with totals and counts
Custom reports people build themselves

nodes.question: Are records grouped into separate projects/workspaces, or is it one shared pool?

options.label: One shared pool — everything lives in one place with filters
Separate projects/workspaces, each with its own members

nodes.question: Who can see a record?

options.label: Everyone in the team sees everything
Records are private to their owner unless shared or assigned
Visible within the owner's team/department; admins see all

nodes.question: Who can change a record?

options.label: Anyone who can see it can edit it
Only its owner/assignee and admins; others just view
Set per record: view / comment / edit

nodes.question: Are the fields on a record fixed, or can admins add their own?

options.label: Fixed — the same fields for everyone
Admins add custom fields (text, number, date, dropdown) to each record type
Admins define whole new record types with their own fields

nodes.question: Are records linked to each other?

options.label: No — each record stands alone
Yes — records of different types reference each other (contact → company → deal)
Yes — including parent/child trees (projects → tasks → sub-tasks)

nodes.question: Should the app do things on its own when records change?

options.label: No — people do everything by hand
Simple rules: when X happens, notify/assign/change stage
Multi-step workflows with conditions and delays

nodes.question: Can two records be the same thing (same email, same serial number)?

options.label: Allowed — nothing stops duplicates
The app warns about likely duplicates and offers to merge
A key field must be unique; duplicates are rejected

nodes.question: How do people find a record?

options.label: Filter and sort within each list
One search box across all record types
Search that also looks inside comments and attachments

nodes.question: Can people change many records at once?

options.label: No — one record at a time
Yes — select many and assign/move/tag/delete together

nodes.question: What happens when a Bookkeeper deletes/renames an Account that already has Transactions and Budgets attached?

options.label: Block deletion while any transaction/budget references it
Force reassigning transactions to another account first
Soft-archive the account but keep historical postings intact

nodes.question: If the same Import File (or a re-upload of the same month) is submitted twice, what happens?

options.label: Detect by name/hash/period and reject the duplicate
Replace the prior import for that period
Append rows, allowing duplicates

nodes.question: How are negative amounts, refunds/credits, and rounding handled so reports stay balanced?

options.label: Store signed integer cents; allow negatives; no rounding
Round only for display, keep full precision internally
Reject negative/zero amounts entirely

nodes.question: How is the Period a Transaction belongs to determined (e.g. a Mar 31 late-night entry, or a backdated invoice)?

options.label: By the transaction's own date field, fixed org timezone
By the period declared on the import file
Bookkeeper assigns the period explicitly

nodes.question: If an Import File passes some rows but fails reconciliation or has bad rows, what state is saved?

options.label: Reject the whole file until it fully reconciles
Load into staging; nothing hits reports until Finance Manager accepts
Commit good rows, flag the bad ones

nodes.question: Can a closed Period be reopened or an approved Monthly Report be un-approved?

options.label: No — closed/approved is final
Finance Manager may reopen, logged in the audit trail
Reopening creates a new versioned revision of the period/report

nodes.question: How is cross-department or delegated access handled (e.g. a Department Head covering another, or Owner drilling into raw transactions)?

options.label: Strict — each head sees only their own department, no delegation
Finance Manager can grant temporary cross-department view
Owner sees all details; heads strictly scoped

nodes.question: When a new import updates figures that were also manually entered (a2) for the same accounts/period, which wins?

options.label: Import is authoritative and overwrites manual entries
Manual entries are preserved; import only adds new rows
Conflicts are flagged for Finance Manager review

cards.context: Sometimes a month you already finalized turns out to need a correction

options.label: Finance Manager may reopen, logged in the audit trail
options.scenario: Your finance manager can reopen a finalized month and fix the numbers directly, and every reopening is stamped with who did it and when.

options.label: No — closed/approved is final
options.scenario: Once a month is finalized, it stays locked for good; any correction has to be recorded in a later, still-open month instead.

options.label: Reopening creates a new versioned revision of the period/report
options.scenario: Reopening a finalized month leaves the original untouched and starts a fresh revision, so you keep both the old and corrected figures side by side.

also_sets: Your books run in one language for one country

cards.context: It's the first Monday of the month and last month's figures still need to be pulled together and reviewed

options.label: Only reminders/notifications
options.scenario: On set days, you and your team get a friendly nudge that a month needs closing or a report needs approving, but nothing is filled in for you.

options.label: Records get created automatically (recurring invoices, appointments, reports)
options.scenario: Each month a fresh monthly summary appears on its own, ready and waiting for your team to check and approve, without anyone starting it by hand.

options.label: No
options.scenario: Nothing happens on its own; your team pulls together, closes, and approves each month's numbers whenever they sit down to do it.

record_custom_fields.context: It's month-end and your bookkeeper asks whether she can track one extra detail on each expense, like a project code.

options.label: Admins add custom fields (text, number, date, dropdown) to each record type
options.scenario: Your staff add their own extra boxes to any record, like a project code or approval date, choosing text, numbers, dates, or a pick-list, whenever a new need comes up.

options.label: Admins define whole new record types with their own fields
options.scenario: Your staff build entirely new kinds of records from scratch, each with its own set of fields, so you can track things the original setup never imagined.

options.label: Fixed — the same fields for everyone
options.scenario: Everyone works with the same set fields on every record, so your figures stay tidy and consistent, but adding a new detail means asking us to change it.

also_sets: Whether each part of the business can shape its own records
That everything runs in one language for one country

x5.context: It's the first of the month and your bookkeeper just uploaded the Excel file, but a few rows don't match the totals

options.label: Commit good rows, flag the bad ones
options.scenario: The clean rows post right away and show up in your numbers, while the mismatched rows sit flagged for someone to fix later.

options.label: Load into staging; nothing hits reports until Finance Manager accepts
options.scenario: Nothing shows in your reports yet; the whole upload waits in a holding area until your Finance Manager reviews and accepts it.

options.label: Reject the whole file until it fully reconciles
options.scenario: The entire file is turned away until every row matches the totals, so your reports only ever move once everything balances.

also_sets: Whether half-finished numbers can appear in your reports
How much your Finance Manager reviews before figures go live
Where a rejected file sends your bookkeeper back to the spreadsheet
